variants: 'Aethiopians' / 'Ethiopians' (Greek and Roman usage for the inhabitants)
entries.note_en: The Greeks, and later the Romans, called the inhabitants of Nubia 'Ethiopians' (GHA II p.231); GHA II p.298 speaks of the 'Aethiopians', 'as the inhabitants of the Kush empire were then generally called'.
The northern Nubian kingdom (Arabic, Nuba), with its capital at Faras; later united with Makuria (GHA III p.194).
The central Nubian kingdom (Arabic, Mukurra), with its capital at Old Dongola (GHA III p.194).
The southern Nubian kingdom, whose northern border lay between the Fifth and Sixth Cataracts, 'with its capital at Soba, in the vicinity of modern-day Khartoum' (GHA III p.196).
Name form only. Links to the Medjay and Blemmyes were removed: no checked source read.
The Funj sultanate, with its capital at Sennar. GHA V p.174: 'the Fundj ruled their domains from Sennār which became their seat of government.'
The Keira (Kayra) dynasty of the Fur, who give Darfur its name. GHA V p.187: 'The Kayra sultanate flourished from about 1640 to 1874.'
entries.badge_note: Founding date: GHA V p.187 'about 1640' vs era start 1650 in data/periods.json.

entries.note_en: A Nuba Mountains kingdom. GHA V p.177: 'the newly established Islamized kingdom of Takali was reduced to subordinate status' by the Fundj. Gleichen 1905 (vol. I p.174) lists Jebel Tagale among the hills 'inhabited by Nubas'.

The state founded by the movement of Muhammad Ahmad al-Mahdi, 'the Mahdiyya' (GHA VII p.73). GHA VII speaks of 'the Mahdist state' and dates its collapse to the Khalifa's defeat at Umm Diwaykrat on 24 November 1899 (pp.77–78).

The joint British-Egyptian regime over the Sudan. Gleichen 1905 (vol. I p.268): 'On 19th January, 1899, an agreement was signed between Great Britain and Egypt, defining the status of the Sudan'. GHA VII p.81 speaks of 'the Condominium government'.

GHA V uses 'central Bilād al-Sūdān' (p.184) and 'western Bilad al-Sudan' (p.190) for regions of the African Sudanic belt. The gloss 'land of the Blacks' and the form 'eastern Bilad al-Sudan' are not in a source read.
